newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SBC GROUP BUYS INTO S.AFRICAN TELKOM - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SBC GROUP BUYS INTO S.AFRICAN TELKOM - REPORT.

text.p: The Johannesburg Sunday Times newspaper said SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd were believed to had won their bid to buy the minority stake in South Africa's Telkom that the government is selling.

"The successful tender for the 30 percent equity stake, which closed at 5 p.m. on Friday London time, is to net the state an estimated six billion rand ($1.34 billion) although some analysts peg the price a bit lower," it said.

The paper gave no source for its report. Telkom and the telecommunications ministry have not even said officially that the tender has closed and could not be reached for comment. The ministry said on Friday it would issue a statement next week.
SBC and Telekom Malaysia have said they intended to bid jointly for a 20 to 30 percent stake in the parastatal in South Africa's first major partial privatisation.
Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom have also been shortlisted as bidders by the government.
The deal, which could value Telkom at more than $4 billion, will be the largest privatisation in Sub-Saharan Africa and just the first major step in the government's privatisation drive.
SBC already has a presence in South Africa through its 15 percent stake in cellular phone operator MTN.
The bids were being handled by SBC Warburg in London.
